# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Admiraal_2019_alemtuzumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Admiraal_2019_alemtuzumab"))$description`
* Article: [Clin Pharmacokinet 2019;58:1609-1620](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-019-00782-0) (open access, PMC6885503). The electronic supplementary material contains the full NONMEM control stream of the final model.

Admiraal et al. described the pharmacokinetics of alemtuzumab (Campath), an
anti-CD52 monoclonal antibody given as serotherapy in the conditioning regimen
of paediatric allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). The final
model is two-compartmental with parallel linear and Michaelis-Menten
elimination from the central compartment. Body weight scales the central volume
(V1) and the intercompartmental clearance (Q) as fixed power functions, and the
linear clearance (CL) through a *body-weight-dependent exponent* (BDE) whose
value itself falls with weight:

$$CL_i = CL_{pop} \cdot \left(\frac{WT}{17.25}\right)^{(a \cdot WT)^b} \cdot e^{\eta_{CL}}$$

The peripheral volume is estimated as a factor of the individual central volume
(V2 = 0.7 x V1). Baseline lymphocyte count was tested and did not affect any
parameter.

# Population

The model was developed from 1146 alemtuzumab concentrations in 206 children
(212 HCTs) treated at Leiden University Medical Center (67 patients, 73 HCTs)
and Great Ormond Street Hospital, London (139 patients) between 2003 and 2015
(Admiraal 2019 Table 1). Median age was 4.8 years (range 0.2-19; 28 infants
younger than 1 year), median weight 17.2 kg (IQR 11-32), and 67% were male. The
most common indication was immune deficiency (52%), followed by haematologic
malignancy (25%) and bone marrow failure (18%). Alemtuzumab was infused
intravenously, usually as 0.2 mg/kg/day on 4-5 consecutive days starting a
median of 8 days before graft infusion; 54% of patients received a cumulative
0.9-1.1 mg/kg and 35% less than 0.9 mg/kg. Race was not reported.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Admiraal_2019_alemtuzumab")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value below is also recorded as an in-file comment next to the matching
`ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Admiraal_2019_alemtuzumab.R`. ESM
denotes the NONMEM control stream (run28) in the electronic supplementary
material.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment, IV, parallel linear + Michaelis-Menten CL from central | n/a | Results 3.2; ESM `$DES` |
| `lcl` (linear CL at 17.25 kg) | log(0.25 L/day) | Table 2 `CL pop`; ESM THETA(1) |
| `e_wt_cl_bdecoef` (a) | 0.038 1/kg | Table 2 `a`; ESM THETA(7) |
| `e_wt_cl_bdeexp` (b) | -0.79 | Table 2 `b`; ESM THETA(8) |
| BDE form `(WT/17.25)^((a*WT)^b)` | n/a | Methods Eq. 7; Table 2; ESM `TVCL = THETA(1) * (MWT**((THETA(7)*WT)**THETA(8)))` |
| `lvc` (V1 at 17.25 kg) | log(2.13 L) | Table 2 `V1,pop`; ESM THETA(2) |
| `e_wt_vc` (c) | 0.58 | Table 2 `c`; ESM THETA(9) |
| `lvp_ratio` (V2 / V1) | log(0.7) | Table 2 `V2,pop (factor of V1)`; ESM `V2 = V1 * THETA(3)` |
| `lq` (Q at 17.25 kg) | log(0.18 L/day) | Table 2 `Q`; ESM THETA(4) |
| `e_wt_q` (d) | 0.74 | Table 2 `d`; ESM THETA(10) |
| `lvmax` | log(0.42 mg/day) | Table 2 `Vmax,pop (AU/day)`; ESM THETA(5) |
| `lkm` | log(1.38 mg/L) | Table 2 `Km,pop (AU/L)`; ESM THETA(6) |
| Reference weight | 17.25 kg | ESM `MWT = WT/17.25` |
| `etalcl` | 0.73314 (104% CV) | Table 2 IIV on CL |
| `etalvc` | 0.33426 (63% CV) | Table 2 IIV on V1 |
| `etalkm` | 1.06623 (138% CV) | Table 2 IIV on Km |
| No IIV on Q, V2 (other than through V1) or Vmax | n/a | ESM `$PK` (`Q = TVQ`, `VMAX = TVVMAX`) |
| `expSd` | 0.34 | Table 2 `Proportional residual error (%)` = 34; ESM `$ERROR` `Y = IPRED + ERR(1)` on log-transformed data |

# Body-weight-dependent exponent on linear clearance

The paper reports that the exponent "varied from 3.69 in children with a body
weight of 5 kg to 0.41 in patients weighing 80 kg" (Results 3.3, electronic
supplementary Fig. S3), and that linear CL "is expected to slightly decrease
from a body weight of 60 kg onwards (decrease of 1.2%)" (Discussion). Both
follow deterministically from the packaged `ini()` values.

```{r bde}
mod <- readModelDb("Admiraal_2019_alemtuzumab")
ini_vals <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta

bde <- tibble(WT = seq(3, 90, by = 0.5)) |>
  mutate(
    exponent = (ini_vals[["e_wt_cl_bdecoef"]] * WT)^ini_vals[["e_wt_cl_bdeexp"]],
    cl_linear = exp(ini_vals[["lcl"]]) * (WT / 17.25)^exponent
  )

exponent_at <- function(wt) {
  (ini_vals[["e_wt_cl_bdecoef"]] * wt)^ini_vals[["e_wt_cl_bdeexp"]]
}
cl_at <- function(wt) exp(ini_vals[["lcl"]]) * (wt / 17.25)^exponent_at(wt)

bde_check <- tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "Exponent at 5 kg",
    "Exponent at 80 kg",
    "Change in linear CL, 60 to 80 kg (%)"
  ),
  Published = c(3.69, 0.41, -1.2),
  Model = c(exponent_at(5), exponent_at(80), 100 * (cl_at(80) / cl_at(60) - 1))
)
knitr::kable(bde_check, digits = 3)

# The published figures were computed from unrounded estimates; a and b are
# printed to two significant figures, so agreement is to that rounding only.
stopifnot(
  abs(bde_check$Model[1] / 3.69 - 1) < 0.02,
  abs(bde_check$Model[2] / 0.41 - 1) < 0.03,
  round(bde_check$Model[3], 1) %in% c(-1.2, -1.3)
)
```

```{r fig-s3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5, fig.cap = "Replicates electronic supplementary Fig. S3 of Admiraal 2019: (A) the BDE scaling exponent on linear CL and (B) typical linear CL, both against body weight."}
bde |>
  pivot_longer(c(exponent, cl_linear), names_to = "quantity") |>
  mutate(
    quantity = factor(
      quantity,
      levels = c("exponent", "cl_linear"),
      labels = c("A: scaling exponent (a x WT)^b", "B: typical linear CL (L/day)")
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(WT, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~quantity, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Body weight (kg)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Contribution of linear and saturable clearance

Total clearance at concentration C is the linear CL plus the instantaneous
Michaelis-Menten clearance V~max~ / (K~m~ + C). The figure reproduces electronic
supplementary Fig. S2 for the 17.25 kg reference child.

```{r fig-s2, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Replicates electronic supplementary Fig. S2 of Admiraal 2019: typical total, linear and saturable clearance against serum alemtuzumab concentration (17.25 kg child)."}
cl_conc <- tibble(conc = 10^seq(-2, 1.3, length.out = 200)) |>
  mutate(
    Linear = exp(ini_vals[["lcl"]]),
    Saturable = exp(ini_vals[["lvmax"]]) / (exp(ini_vals[["lkm"]]) + conc),
    Total = Linear + Saturable
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-conc, names_to = "pathway", values_to = "cl")

ggplot(cl_conc, aes(conc, cl, linetype = pathway)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Linear = "dotdash", Saturable = "dashed", Total = "solid")) +
  labs(x = "Alemtuzumab concentration (mg/L)", y = "Clearance (L/day)", linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw()

# At concentrations far below Km the saturable pathway approaches Vmax/Km.
stopifnot(abs(
  exp(ini_vals[["lvmax"]]) / (exp(ini_vals[["lkm"]]) + 1e-6) -
    exp(ini_vals[["lvmax"]] - ini_vals[["lkm"]])
) < 1e-6)
```

# Virtual cohort

Observed data are not public. The virtual cohort draws body weight from a
log-normal distribution with the published median (17.2 kg) and a spread that
reproduces the published interquartile range (11-32 kg), truncated to 3-90 kg.
Every subject receives the most common regimen, 0.2 mg/kg/day on five
consecutive days (cumulative 1 mg/kg), with day 0 the first infusion as in
Fig. 1 of the paper. Infusion duration is not reported; 4 hours is assumed.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2019)
n_sub <- 200
wt_sdlog <- (log(32) - log(11)) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))

cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, log(17.2), wt_sdlog), 3), 90)
) |>
  mutate(
    wt_band = cut(
      WT,
      breaks = c(0, 11, 17.3, 32, Inf),
      labels = c("<11 kg", "11-17.3 kg", "17.3-32 kg", ">32 kg"),
      right = FALSE
    )
  )

dose_days <- 0:4
# Includes the bin times digitised from Fig. 4e below.
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 6, by = 0.125),
  seq(6.5, 14, by = 0.5),
  seq(15, 80, by = 1),
  c(21.5, 28.5, 53.5)
)))

dose_rows <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = dose_days) |>
  mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 0.2 * WT, dur = 4 / 24, cmt = "central")
obs_rows <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central")
events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

table(cohort$wt_band)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("WT", "wt_band"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
# Concentrations at the observation records only (evid is not returned).
sim <- sim |> filter(!is.na(Cc))

# Population predictions (no between-subject or residual variability) for
# the prediction correction below.
pred <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = events,
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, pred = Cc)
```

## Prediction-corrected VPC (Figure 4e)

Fig. 4e of the paper is a prediction-corrected VPC on a log axis. Its simulated
median falls about 3-fold between days 15 and 50, far less than the terminal
half-life of the typical patient (about 8 days at low concentrations) allows.
The flattening appears once simulated values below the 0.1 ug/mL limit of
quantification are removed before the percentiles are taken, which is the usual
way a VPC with an LLOQ is built. Only the subjects whose concentrations remain
measurable then contribute late in the profile. The chunk below repeats the
prediction correction (each simulated value scaled by the bin median of the
population prediction over the subject's own population prediction) with and
without that censoring. It overlays the simulated percentiles digitised from
Fig. 4e (dotted lines in the paper; read from the raster at about +/-10%).

```{r fig-vpc, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Replicates the simulated percentiles of Fig. 4e of Admiraal 2019 (prediction-corrected VPC). Lines: 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the simulated concentrations including residual error, after removing simulated values below the 0.1 ug/mL LLOQ (solid) or keeping them (dashed). Points: the paper's simulated percentiles, digitised."}
lloq <- 0.1

pc_percentiles <- function(d) {
  d |>
    group_by(time) |>
    mutate(pc = sim * median(pred) / pred) |>
    summarise(
      p05 = quantile(pc, 0.05),
      p50 = quantile(pc, 0.50),
      p95 = quantile(pc, 0.95),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

sim_pred <- sim |>
  select(id, time, sim) |>
  left_join(pred, by = c("id", "time")) |>
  filter(time > 0)

vpc <- bind_rows(
  sim_pred |> filter(sim >= lloq) |> pc_percentiles() |> mutate(censoring = "Below LLOQ removed"),
  sim_pred |> pc_percentiles() |> mutate(censoring = "All simulated values")
)

# Simulated (dotted) percentiles of Fig. 4e, read from the published figure.
fig4e <- tibble(
  time = c(4.5, 10.5, 15, 21.5, 28.5, 36, 47, 53.5),
  p05 = c(0.98, 0.143, 0.103, 0.086, 0.052, 0.065, 0.033, 0.034),
  p50 = c(4.0, 1.46, 0.96, 0.65, 0.54, 0.42, 0.31, 0.32),
  p95 = c(13.4, 6.4, 5.1, 3.6, 3.3, 2.96, 2.45, 2.45)
)

vpc_long <- vpc |>
  pivot_longer(c(p05, p50, p95), names_to = "percentile")
fig4e_long <- fig4e |>
  pivot_longer(c(p05, p50, p95), names_to = "percentile")

ggplot(vpc_long, aes(time, value, group = interaction(percentile, censoring))) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = censoring)) +
  geom_point(data = fig4e_long, aes(group = percentile, shape = percentile)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Below LLOQ removed" = "solid", "All simulated values" = "dashed")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 60), ylim = c(1e-2, 30)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first alemtuzumab dose (days)",
    y = "Prediction-corrected alemtuzumab (mg/L)",
    linetype = NULL,
    shape = "Fig. 4e"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r vpc-check}
vpc_cmp <- vpc |>
  filter(censoring == "Below LLOQ removed") |>
  inner_join(fig4e, by = "time", suffix = c("_sim", "_paper")) |>
  mutate(ratio_p50 = p50_sim / p50_paper)

vpc_cmp |>
  select(time, p50_sim, p50_paper, ratio_p50, p95_sim, p95_paper) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Day" = time,
    "Median, simulated" = p50_sim,
    "Median, Fig. 4e" = p50_paper,
    "Ratio" = ratio_p50,
    "95th pct, simulated" = p95_sim,
    "95th pct, Fig. 4e" = p95_paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

late_uncensored <- vpc |>
  filter(censoring == "All simulated values", time %in% c(47, 53.5))
late_censored <- vpc |>
  filter(censoring == "Below LLOQ removed", time %in% c(47, 53.5))

stopifnot(
  # Centre: the censored median tracks the paper's simulated median over the
  # whole profile (typical ratio within 35%), which a wrong clearance, volume
  # or Michaelis-Menten constant would not.
  abs(log(median(vpc_cmp$ratio_p50))) < log(1.35),
  # The late flattening in Fig. 4e comes from the censoring: without it the
  # late median is several-fold lower.
  all(late_censored$p50 > 3 * late_uncensored$p50)
)
```

The typical-value profiles below show the non-linear influence of weight under
uniform mg/kg dosing that motivates the paper's conclusion: larger children
reach higher peaks because V1 rises less than proportionally with weight
(exponent 0.58), while in the smallest children the linear pathway is almost
absent and elimination is dominated by the saturable pathway.

```{r typical, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Typical concentration-time profiles (no between-subject variability) for children of 5, 11, 17.25, 32 and 60 kg receiving 0.2 mg/kg/day for 5 days."}
typical_wt <- c(5, 11, 17.25, 32, 60)
typical_events <- tibble(id = seq_along(typical_wt), WT = typical_wt) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = dose_days) |>
  mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 0.2 * WT, dur = 4 / 24, cmt = "central") |>
  bind_rows(
    tibble(id = seq_along(typical_wt), WT = typical_wt) |>
      tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
      mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

typical <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = typical_events,
  keep = "WT",
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))

ggplot(typical, aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(WT))) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1e-2, 20)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first alemtuzumab dose (days)",
    y = "Alemtuzumab (mg/L)",
    colour = "Weight (kg)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA is run per subject over the full 80-day profile with weight quartile band
(the bands of Fig. 2 of the paper) as the grouping variable.

```{r pknca}
# Integrator noise can leave a tail value a hair below zero; assert it is noise,
# floor it, and drop the numerically-zero tail so the half-life fit does not
# follow it (rising-phase points are kept).
stopifnot(all(sim$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim$Cc), na.rm = TRUE))
conc_df <- sim |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  filter(time <= time[which.max(Cc)] | Cc >= 1e-6 * max(Cc)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(id, time, Cc, wt_band)

dose_df <- dose_rows |>
  select(id, time, amt, wt_band)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | wt_band + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | wt_band + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = 80,
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(wt_band, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

nca_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Weight band" = wt_band,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (day)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-80 (mg*day/L)" = auclast,
    "t1/2 (day)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters by weight band, 0.2 mg/kg/day for 5 days.")
```

The paper does not tabulate NCA parameters, so there is no published value to
compare against. The structural check below asserts the weight gradient the
paper describes for uniform mg/kg dosing, on cohort medians: peak concentration
rises from the lightest to the heaviest quartile (Cmax per mg/kg scales roughly
as WT^0.42 through V1), and the peak falls on the last infusion day.

```{r pknca-check}
by_band <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax")) |>
  group_by(wt_band, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

stopifnot(
  by_band$cmax[by_band$wt_band == ">32 kg"] >
    1.5 * by_band$cmax[by_band$wt_band == "<11 kg"],
  all(by_band$tmax > 4 & by_band$tmax < 5)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Reference weight.** The control stream normalises weight by 17.25 kg; the
  Table 2 footnote prints 17.3 kg and Table 1 a median of 17.2 kg. The code value
  (17.25 kg) is used.
* **Vmax and Km units.** Table 2 prints Vmax in "AU/day" and Km in "AU/L". Doses
  were in mg/kg and both assays report concentrations in ug/mL (= mg/L), so the
  only unit-consistent reading is mg/day and mg/L; the model uses those units.
* **Between-subject variability.** Table 2 reports IIV as a percentage without
  stating how it was derived from the NONMEM variance, and the `$OMEGA` initial
  estimates in the control stream (2, 1, 2) are round values that do not hint
  at a previous run. The library's convention omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) is used
  (CL 0.733, V1 0.334, Km 1.066). If the percentages were instead
  100 x sqrt(omega^2), the variances would be 1.082, 0.397 and 1.904. The
  bootstrap percentile ranges cannot decide between the readings, because a
  percentile maps through either transform unchanged. Against Fig. 4e, the
  simulated 95th percentile is low at late times under both readings, by more
  under this one (about 45% low at days 28-47, against about 27% low under the
  other reading in a 3000-subject run). But the paper's band is already about
  twice as wide as either reading at day 4.5 (95th / 5th percentile ratio about
  14, against 7 under both readings), where the IIV scale barely matters, which
  points to the
  unpublished dosing design (cumulative doses 0.2-1.5 mg/kg, varied start days,
  graft-bag doses) rather than the IIV scale. The comparison is therefore not
  used to choose between them.
* **Residual error.** The model was fit to log-transformed concentrations with
  an additive error (`Y = IPRED + ERR(1)`), which the paper reports as a 34%
  proportional error. It is encoded as `lnorm(expSd)` with `expSd = 0.34`.
* **Infusion duration** is not reported; 4 hours is assumed for every infusion.
  On the daily time scale of the model this affects only the first hours after
  each infusion.
* **Virtual cohort.** Weight is drawn log-normally from the published median and
  IQR; age, sex and diagnosis do not enter the model and are not simulated. All
  subjects receive the modal regimen of 0.2 mg/kg/day for 5 days; the 0.5 mg/kg
  cumulative regimens and graft-bag administration are not simulated.
* **Fig. 1 Km line.** The dashed Km line in Fig. 1 is drawn at about 2 mg/L,
  whereas Table 2 and the control stream give 1.38 mg/L. Electronic
  supplementary Fig. S2 (saturable clearance against concentration) matches
  1.38 mg/L and Vmax 0.42 mg/day exactly, so the table value is used.
* **VPC censoring.** The reconstruction of Fig. 4e removes simulated values
  below 0.1 ug/mL before taking percentiles. The paper does not describe how
  its VPC treated the limit of quantification; this choice is inferred from
  the shape of its simulated percentiles.
* **Below-quantification samples** were handled with the M6 method in the
  original analysis; this has no counterpart in a simulation.
